solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: An ape crosses the treetops

indicators.note: the word for ape stretches across, straddling the first word of the clue

parts.note: to ape is to copy, imitate

explanation.surface: A monkey swings its way across the top of the forest.
explanation.definitionFit: The canopy is the upper layer of a forest formed by the crowns of trees.

clue.text: Party therefore has French woman making soup

parts.note: CON, short for the Conservative Party
so means therefore
MME, abbreviation for Madame, a French married woman

explanation.surface: A political group's member brings along a French lady who cooks soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Consommé is a clear broth, a kind of soup.

clue.text: When the third most horrible is changed it can become most fashionable!

indicators.note: points at the third letter of the word for most horrible as the one to alter
says that the chosen letter is swapped for another one

parts.note: nastiest means most horrible

explanation.surface: A playful claim that the ugliest thing can become the smartest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the third ... is changed' swaps the third letter, S, of NASTIEST for T.
explanation.definitionFit: Nattiest means smartest or neatest in dress, so most stylish.

clue.text: Tiny opal possibly worn behind the ears

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters given could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A small opal earring, perhaps, sits behind the ears.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairstyle gathered at the back of the head, so it hangs behind and between the ears.

clue.text: Ship's company entering bar requires particular sort of bottle

indicators.note: the sailors' word goes into the middle of the word for bar

parts.note: to bar is to stop
a ship's company is its crew

explanation.surface: Sailors walk into a pub and want a certain kind of bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A screw-top bottle has a threaded cap rather than a cork, a specific type of closure.

clue.text: Dogtooth

parts.note: split into dog and tooth: the adjective for dogs and the pointed tooth near the front

explanation.surface: A single word naming a pattern or a tooth.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the word as two: 'dog' gives the adjective, 'tooth' the pointed tooth also called an eye tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: The word serves both as the adjective for dogs and as a pointed tooth, exactly what the compound says.

clue.text: Laxative packaged with remarkable meticulousness

indicators.note: the letters sit wrapped within the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A medicine wrapped up with great care.
explanation.definitionFit: Loosely a purgative: strictly an agent that induces vomiting, it purges the gut from the other end.

clue.text: Waver about forwarded message, ignore wife heading north

indicators.note: in a down entry, going north means read from bottom to top

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: ignore means leave out the abbreviation for wife

parts.note: a tweet is a message sent on, by Twitter

explanation.surface: Hesitating over a forwarded message while ignoring a spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignore wife' turns TWEET into TEET; 'heading north' turns RE+TEET backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To teeter is to wobble unsteadily, to hesitate between options.

clue.text: Fruit for dad mid-voyage

parts.note: papa is another word for dad

indicators.note: mid asks for the central letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit for father halfway through a sea trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical fruit with orange flesh, also called pawpaw.

clue.text: Observing that bell is silent?

parts.note: a silent bell makes no ring, so the word no
ting is the sound of a small bell

explanation.surface: Watching to check whether a bell has gone quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Noting is remarking or paying attention to something, as when watching.

clue.text: Want to have backward look around at water level

indicators.note: the reversed look goes round the outside of the word for want
backward says to read the word for look in the other direction

parts.note: a peek is a quick look
want means need

explanation.surface: Wishing to glance back while wading around at the water's edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes water rising to one's knees, so the surface sits at that height.

clue.text: Old privateer has no right to drug

indicators.note: has no means the abbreviation for right is removed

parts.note: a privateer is a licensed pirate

explanation.surface: A historic buccaneer with no rights turns to narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: An opiate is a narcotic derived from opium.

clue.text: Everything is about body holding on

indicators.note: the word for body contains the short word for about

parts.note: an entity is a body, a thing with separate existence
re means about

explanation.surface: Something about a body hanging on, covering everything.
explanation.definitionFit: The entirety is the whole of something, all of it.

clue.text: Cover for record about awful novel

indicators.note: the record's letters go around the rearranged novel

parts.note: EP is an extended play record

indicators.note: awful signals the letters of novel are mangled

explanation.surface: A record sleeve chosen for a dreadful novel.
explanation.definitionFit: To envelop is to wrap up or cover completely.

clue.text: Bonus earned by Jack Robinson, he of dubious character

indicators.note: dubious character means the preceding letters are in a doubtful, disordered form

explanation.surface: A reward that some shady Jack Robinson picked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dubious character' rearranges ROBINSON HE OF. 'Jack Robinson' looks like a name, but Jack is the card.
explanation.definitionFit: In cribbage, a point scored for holding the jack of the turned-up card's suit.

clue.text: Service provided for Highlands

parts.note: Mass is a church service
if means provided that

explanation.surface: A church service laid on for the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A massif is a compact group of mountains, upland terrain.

clue.text: See 13
See 13
Bloomer liable to crumple without oxygen

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the jumbled letters go around the oxygen symbol
crumpling distorts the word liable into a new shape

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A flower likely to wilt when deprived of air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to crumple' rearranges LIABLE, and 'without' puts it outside O, so L+O+BELIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a flowering plant; lobelia is a bedding flower.

clue.text: Road motor shows muscle reversing on deserted hairpin

parts.note: auto is a motor car

indicators.note: reversing says the muscle's letters run backwards

parts.note: AB is short for abdominal muscle

indicators.note: deserted means emptied, leaving only the outside letters

explanation.surface: A car flexes its muscles as it backs up on an empty hairpin bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns AB into BA; 'deserted' empties hairpin to HN.
explanation.definitionFit: An autobahn is a German motorway, a kind of highway.

clue.text: Deliver across motorway to jogger?

indicators.note: the word for deliver lies across the motorway, around it

parts.note: render means deliver, as in render a verdict
M1 (written MI) is Britain's main north-south motorway

explanation.surface: Handing something to a runner over the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jogger?' is not a runner but something that jogs the memory; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A prompt nudges or jogs someone's memory.

clue.text: Mystery man begins to unravel correspondence

indicators.note: unravelling pulls the letters apart and remakes them
begins takes the opening letter of man

explanation.surface: A mystery man starts to untangle some letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Symmetry is a correspondence of parts on either side of a line, a matching balance.

clue.text: Guarantee fatty will have second breakfast

indicators.note: the word for fatty takes the chosen letter inside it

parts.note: suety means like suet, fatty

indicators.note: second picks the second letter of breakfast

explanation.surface: A greedy person is sure to want a second breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: A surety is a pledge or security given as a promise.

clue.text: Nut regularly mails, day after day

indicators.note: after puts the first day's letter behind the second day
regularly takes every other letter of mails

parts.note: MON is short for Monday

explanation.surface: A nut is posted out, day after day.
explanation.definitionFit: The almond is an edible nut from a tree of the rose family.

clue.text: With which Rumpole represents boxers?

definitions.meaning: Rumpole is a fictional barrister; barristers take instructions in legal documents to represent clients
boxers are loose underpants; another style of underpants is the close-fitting kind

explanation.surface: A TV barrister defending prizefighters.
explanation.walkthrough: Rumpole of the Bailey is a British TV barrister.
explanation.definitionFit: Briefs are both a barrister's case instructions and men's underwear.

clue.text: United more certain he's a rip-off merchant

parts.note: surer means more certain

explanation.surface: A football fan is convinced someone is a con man.
explanation.definitionFit: A usurer lends money at extortionate interest, a swindler.

clue.text: See 13
Naomi, Catherine and Tracy are disheartened by subtlety

indicators.note: losing the heart leaves just the first and last letters of each name

explanation.surface: Three women are dispirited by some subtle point.
explanation.definitionFit: A nicety is a fine distinction, a subtle detail.

clue.text: Cricket ground takes joint title

parts.note: Lord's is the famous cricket ground in London
the hip is a joint

explanation.surface: A cricket ground takes a shared name.
explanation.definitionFit: A form of address for a peer or judge, an honorific.

clue.text: Platform for quiet disapproval

parts.note: P is piano, quiet in music
odium is general disapproval or hatred

explanation.surface: A stage set up for silent protest.
explanation.definitionFit: A podium is a raised stand for a speaker or winner.

clue.text: Handicapped law-breaker traced to amusement arcade

definitions.note: means something that is found in an arcade

parts.note: having only one arm describes a disability
a bandit is an outlaw

explanation.surface: A disabled criminal is tracked down to a games arcade.
explanation.definitionFit: A slot machine with a lever, the classic arcade gambling machine.

clue.text: See 28
Devastates two guys on the Sabbath

parts.note: Des and Troy, two men's names
S is short for Sunday, the Christian Sabbath

explanation.surface: A pair of men wreck things on a Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: To destroy is to ruin or wreck completely.

clue.text: Go for revitalised green youth leader

indicators.note: revitalised suggests green's letters given new form
leader takes the first letter of youth

explanation.surface: Choosing a reinvigorated environmentalist youth leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Go means vigour or drive, as in full of go.
